summary: npm package uses exports subpath hijack to execute setup.js and drop an exfil handler at /tmp/h.tsx
details: The package's `exports` field maps the `./package.json` subpath to `setup.js`, so any consumer resolving `require('z-deno-truth-bwhlsz/package.json')` executes JavaScript instead of reading the manifest. `setup.js` writes a Deno/Hono handler to `/tmp/h.tsx` that reads `/readflag`, `/flagserver`, `/app/backdoor.tsx`, and `/entrypoint.sh` from the host filesystem and returns their contents in the HTTP response, matching on a `hitcon{...}` pattern. The exports subpath hijack turns routine package-metadata resolution into arbitrary code execution on the installer, and the dropped file is a shipped exfiltration handler intended to be picked up by a Deno server on the host. While the file-read targets are specific to a CTF environment, the delivery mechanism (subpath hijack + filesystem drop) executes on any host that resolves the package's `./package.json` subpath.
